clue.text: Fruit's earlier around lake, reportedly widespread

indicators.note: around tells us the word for earlier wraps itself about the abbreviation for lake

parts.note: back means earlier, as in 'back in the day'
L is the standard map abbreviation for lake

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the next word is only heard, not spelt, so we take its sound

parts.note: current means widespread or prevalent, as in 'a current belief'

explanation.surface: Someone describes a fruit, said to be an earlier variety that grew widely around a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts L inside BACK to give BLACK; 'reportedly' turns CURRENT into its sound-alike, the dried-fruit spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: This dark berry grows on a bush and is a common soft fruit, used in jams and cordials.

clue.text: Birds creating stirs around isle

indicators.note: around shows the verb meaning stirs is wrapped about the letter for isle

parts.note: budges means stirs or shifts slightly
I is the usual abbreviation for isle or island

explanation.surface: A flock of birds is stirring things up all over an island.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small parakeets, kept widely as caged pet birds.

clue.text: HM turned up in one part — part of Ulster, say

parts.note: A means one, as in 'a single item'

indicators.note: in tells us the turned letters sit inside the phrase built from one and part

parts.note: a role is a part played by an actor

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Her Majesty turns up to play a part in a province of Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: An Ulster is a long loose overcoat as well as the province; 'turned up' reads HM upwards before it goes in, and 'say' marks the coat as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening in a coat or shirt through which the arm goes is a piece of any sleeved garment.

clue.text: Boost for good-time girl after thrills

indicators.note: after places the word for good-time girl behind the word for thrills

parts.note: kicks are thrills, as in 'doing it for kicks'
tart is a slang term for a promiscuous good-time girl

explanation.surface: A good-time girl gets a boost after some thrills.
explanation.definitionFit: To give an engine or project a sudden start is to boost it into action.

clue.text: It doesn't exactly stick in one's throat, but it's close

definitions.text: It doesn't exactly stick in one's throat, but it's close

parts.words: It doesn't exactly stick in one's throat, but it's close
parts.note: plays on the idiom for something hard to accept, while describing a fleshy lobe that hangs at the back of the mouth, near the throat

explanation.definitionFit: The fleshy lobe hanging from the soft palate dangles just above the throat.

clue.text: The rest have digs outside University

indicators.note: outside shows the verb for having digs goes around the abbreviation for university

parts.note: to reside is to live somewhere, as students in digs (lodgings) do

explanation.surface: The remaining students have lodgings away from the university.
explanation.walkthrough: Digs is British slang for rented lodgings, often a student's.
explanation.definitionFit: What is left over after the main part is removed is the remainder.

clue.text: Bit of a nerve?

parts.note: sounds like a remark about cheek, but literally asks for a cell that makes up part of nervous tissue

explanation.definitionFit: Nerves are made of bundles of these signalling cells, so each is a piece of nervous tissue.

clue.text: Forecaster working under pressure?

parts.note: suggests a stressed meteorologist, but describes an instrument that predicts weather by measuring air pressure

explanation.definitionFit: A barometer forecasts the weather by responding to changes in atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Sort of disease calling for nasty medicine one rejected?

indicators.note: nasty suggests the letters of medicine are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A doctor asks what kind of illness calls for a foul-tasting remedy that the patient refused.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'medicine' are the answer plus I ('one'), which is 'rejected', so drop I and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease that is regularly found in a given region or population is described with this term.

clue.text: A Parisian, facing test, proves shaky

parts.note: un is French for 'a', as a Parisian would say it
to sound is to test, as in sounding out an idea or the depth of water

explanation.surface: A Frenchman facing an exam turns out to be nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Something weak or unreliable, such as a structure or argument, is shaky.

clue.text: Liability for ruined gate (after I'd reversed blue vehicle)

indicators.note: after puts the reworked gate behind the bracketed pieces
reversed tells us the letters of I'd are written backwards

parts.note: blue means sad or low in spirits
a van is a road vehicle

indicators.note: ruined shows the letters of gate are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A ruined gate became a liability after someone reversed a blue van into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' makes DI from I'd; 'ruined' rearranges GATE into TAGE, which goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A liability is a drawback or handicap, something that puts one at a weaker position.

clue.text: Sorting out figures

indicators.note: out, as in 'sorting out', shows the letters of the word are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone is busy arranging some numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorting out' reads as the whole phrase for arranging, but 'Sorting' is the fodder and 'out' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: These are triangles, three-sided geometric shapes.

clue.text: Tough for couple in a Latin country

indicators.note: in shows the word for couple sits inside the letters for a Latin country

parts.note: rus is the Latin word for the countryside
a duo is a couple or pair

explanation.surface: Life is hard for a married couple in a Latin American country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin country' looks like Spain or Italy, but it means the Latin word for country, RUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard, laborious task demands great effort.

clue.text: Points to petition obtaining result

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north
to sue is to petition or appeal, as in suing for peace

explanation.surface: Points made in a petition achieve a result.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow as a consequence is to result.

clue.text: Nick twig

definitions.meaning: to nick is British slang for arrest a criminal
to twig is British slang for understand or grasp

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to arrest someone and to grasp an idea.

clue.text: Puerto Rico playing host to poor R Crusoe's antecedent

indicators.note: playing host to means the letters for Puerto Rico take in the other piece
poor shows the letters of R Crusoe are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Puerto Rico welcomes poor Robinson Crusoe's ancestor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges R CRUSOE into ECURSOR, which goes inside PR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that comes before and leads to a later thing is a forerunner.

clue.text: Swear word

definitions.meaning: to swear is to promise solemnly
one's word is a promise or pledge, as in 'I give you my word'

explanation.definitionFit: The term means both to promise solemnly and a pledge or assurance.

clue.text: Union gets a periodical strike set up

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means these letters read upwards

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, a periodical
to lam is to strike or thrash

explanation.surface: A trade union gets a magazine article about a strike published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns the periodical-plus-strike pair upwards as one block, which then follows A.
explanation.definitionFit: A blend or combination of things is a union of them.

clue.text: A figure consuming Italian drug

indicators.note: consuming means the shape takes the abbreviation for Italian inside it

parts.note: a cone is a solid geometric figure
It is short for Italian, as in Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: A celebrity is taking an Italian drug.
explanation.walkthrough: Aconite (monkshood) is a poisonous plant used as a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Aconite yields a poison once used medicinally as a sedative.

clue.text: Follow academic's teaching

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
MA, Master of Arts, is an academic degree holder

explanation.surface: Someone is told to follow a professor's lectures.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrine or set of principles laid down by an authority is its teaching.

clue.text: Attempt to cover wrinkles up in alarm?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole construction reads from bottom to top
to cover means the word for attempt goes around the word for wrinkles

parts.note: a bid is an attempt
ruts are grooves or furrows, like wrinkles

explanation.surface: Someone tries to hide wrinkles with make-up, worried about looking old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the whole container over, read bottom to top. The question mark shows alarm used as a verb, to upset.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouble or upset someone is to alarm them.

clue.text: Hard stuff from Ulster kept in jar

indicators.note: kept in means the letters for Ulster are held inside the verb for jar

parts.note: to grate is to jar, as a noise grates on the nerves
NI is Northern Ireland, often called Ulster

explanation.surface: Whisky from Northern Ireland is stored in a jar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard stuff' suggests strong spirits, but it means a hard stone.
explanation.definitionFit: This igneous rock is notably tough, a hard material used for building.

clue.text: Seaman with a unique sea ear?

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
lone means single or unique

explanation.surface: A sailor with an unusual ear for the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The shellfish is also called the sea ear for its ear-shaped shell.
explanation.definitionFit: This edible shellfish has an ear-shaped shell lined with mother-of-pearl.

clue.text: Aristocrats, displaying adornments, beheaded

indicators.note: beheaded means the word for adornments loses its first letter

parts.note: pearls are jewels worn as adornments

explanation.surface: Aristocrats wearing their jewels are executed.
explanation.definitionFit: These are noblemen ranking above viscounts in the British peerage.

clue.text: Bit of a pretender with a strut, maybe

definitions.text: Bit of a pretender with a strut, maybe

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters might be arranged another way
bit of means just the first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A pretender to status swaggers about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges P (first of 'pretender') with A STRUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has risen suddenly and behaves arrogantly is a self-important pretender to position.

clue.text: Address in Italy having doubtful origins

indicators.note: doubtful suggests the letters of the word are uncertain in order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone of uncertain descent lives at an Italian address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' is a form of address, a title, not a street location.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian title equivalent to Mr or Sir is a form of address.

clue.text: Celebrate about old city reaching a turning point?

indicators.note: about means the word for celebrate goes round the other letters

parts.note: to sing is to celebrate, as in singing someone's praises
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: People celebrate around an ancient city at a pivotal moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Milk that is going off is said to turn; the question mark flags that pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk going off is said to be turning, so this sense plays on that.

clue.text: Vast sublime area spread around heart of Wyoming

indicators.note: around shows the rearranged letters wrap the central letter
spread suggests the letters are scattered into a new arrangement
heart of means the middle letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A vast sublime area spreads around central Wyoming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges the eleven letters of the two fodder words; 'around' wraps them round the centre letter of Wyoming.
explanation.definitionFit: Something too large to be measured is boundless.
